output.brief: The rejects come from a combination: Arnholt resin dried in Press 5's dryer (D5), which is degraded. It is not the new operators and not Arnholt in general. On Press 5, Arnholt runs about 10% rejects against 0.9% for Quillan. On Press 7, Arnholt runs 0.8%. The six new hires reject at the same rate as experienced operators. Second shift looks worse only because all its VX runs on Press 5. D5's dew point is about −16 to −19 °C, and its alarm limit was loosened in week 31. Quillan resin starts drier, so it survived. Arnholt arrives wetter, at 0.27–0.33% at the dryer inlet, and D5 can't bring it under the 0.20% limit. The same Arnholt lot dried in a good portable dryer gave 0.8% rejects, against 10.4% through D5. So the cause is well established. What isn't known is why Arnholt arrives wetter. It may be north-annex storage or the supplier, and the samples can't separate the two. Do this week: repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore the alarm limit, keep Arnholt off D5 until verified, and add a feed-throat moisture check for every lot. Don't discipline the operators or drop Arnholt. Hold off on renting space until a conditioned-storage test of the annex is done. Reply to the 8D with this finding.
